title: Gomes-Júnior, A. R., Morgado, B. E., Benedetti-Rossi, G. et al. (2022). SORA: Stellar Occultation Reduction and Analysis. MNRAS 511, 1167-1181 (arXiv:2201.01799)
note: Read in full from the arXiv LaTeX source. Source of the closest-approach equations (Assafin et al. 2010 geometry), the shadow velocity, the magnitude-drop equation, the Fresnel scale f = sqrt(lambda D / 2), the star radius at the body, the exposure length r_t = V_S t_exp, the timing uncertainty sigma_t = sigma_LC t_exp / Delta f, the tangent-plane equations 6 to 9, the 0.021 s light-time and the chord and ellipse chi-square. Its printed albedo equation omits the factor 0.4 that the code applies.

title: riogroup/SORA, Stellar Occultation Reduction and Analysis, version 0.3.3, commit 63a1b2d of 2026-08-03
note: Code read: sora/prediction/core.py (occ_params and prediction), sora/prediction/occmap.py (xy2latlon and the path and 1-sigma lines), sora/lightcurve/utils.py (calc_fresnel, bar_fresnel, calc_magnitude_drop), sora/lightcurve/core.py (occ_model), sora/occultation/utils.py (calc_geometric_albedo) and sora/occultation/fitting.py (fit_ellipse). The authors document their own library, so the grade is company.

title: Herald, D., Gault, D., Anderson, R. et al. (2020). Precise astrometry and diameters of asteroids from occultations: a data set of observations and their interpretation. MNRAS 499, 4570-4590 (arXiv:2010.06086)
note: Read sections 1 to 6, 8 and 10 to 11 from the arXiv LaTeX source. Source of the reduction on the fundamental plane with Besselian elements and a cubic shadow motion, the inverse Besselian astrometry steps, the single-chord uncertainty rules, the weights 5, 4, 3 and 1, the ellipse-fit treatment of misses, the 40 mas and 40 km pre-Gaia statement, the 586 events of 2019, the Gaia DR2 bright-star frame rotation and the 10 ms timing goal.

title: Ferreira, J. F., Tanga, P., Spoto, F., Machado, P. and Herald, D. (2022). Asteroid astrometry by stellar occultations: accuracy of the existing sample from orbital fitting. A&A 658, A73 (arXiv:2201.03892)
note: Read from the arXiv text. Source of the pre-Gaia residual level of 30 to 50 mas, the Gaia EDR3 level near 10 mas, the factor of about 5 reduction, the 10 mas FWHM of the residual core, the 3 to 4 mas along-track error level, the RUWE analysis and the statement that 61 per cent of events are single-chord.

title: Desmars, J., Camargo, J. I. B., Braga-Ribas, F. et al. (2015). Orbit determination of trans-Neptunian objects and Centaurs for the prediction of stellar occultations. A&A 584, A96 (arXiv:1509.08674)
note: Read from the arXiv LaTeX source. Source of the NIMA least-squares correction, the covariance propagation Lambda(t) = A(t) Lambda_0 A(t)^T, the weighting omega_i^2 = N_i b_i^2 + sigma_i^2, the bias table (300 mas for MPC data, 75 to 300 mas for offset data, 0 for occultations) and the result that the constant-offset method failed for 6 of 13 events.

title: Lucky Star project. NIMA ephemerides README.txt (version history 1 to 4)
note: Read in full. Lists the weighting of each NIMA version, the occultation sigma of 40 or 75 mas, and the version 4 rule for offsets reduced with Gaia DR1: bias = 40 + 20 |yr - 2015| mas and sigma = 20 + 20 |yr - 2015| mas, in use since 2016-12-07. The file carries no later version.

title: Lucky Star project. Predictions of stellar occultations by TNOs, Centaurs and Trojans (web page)
note: Read. States that ephemerides come from NIMA, star positions and proper motions from Gaia DR3, satellites from the Genoid project, and defines the normalised magnitude G* = G + 2.5 log(v/20) with v the sky-plane velocity in km/s.

title: Tanga, P. and Delbo, M. (2007). Asteroid occultations today and tomorrow: toward the GAIA era. A&A 474, 1015-1022 (arXiv:0801.2684)
note: Read the sections on astrometric accuracy from the arXiv LaTeX source. Source of sigma_path = sqrt(sigma_CEU^2 + sigma_star^2), the efficiency factor p = 2 theta / sigma_path, the pre-Gaia catalogue errors (FK6 1 mas, Hipparcos 10 mas, Tycho-2 70 mas, UCAC2 20 mas), the 0.5 arcsec ephemeris and 350 km statement, and the 15 per cent success rate of 2005.

title: Gaia Collaboration, David, P., Mignard, F. et al. (2023). Gaia Focused Product Release: asteroid orbital solution. Properties and assessment. A&A 680, A37 (arXiv:2310.14699)
note: Read section 5.6 and the abstract in the arXiv version. Source of the orbits of nearly 157 000 asteroids from Gaia data alone, the comparison with 5 774 occultation positions of 978 asteroids, the O-C peak near 10 mas for events in 2014 to 2020, and the degradation of about 10 mas per year outside the Gaia arc.

title: Rommel, F. L., Braga-Ribas, F., Desmars, J. et al. (2020). Stellar occultations enable milliarcsecond astrometry for Trans-Neptunian objects and Centaurs. A&A 644, A40 (arXiv:2010.12708)
note: Abstract and method summary read. Source of the 37 positions for 19 TNOs and 4 Centaurs, 68 per cent single-chord, at sub-milliarcsecond intrinsic precision on the Gaia DR2 frame.

title: Camargo, J. I. B., Desmars, J., Braga-Ribas, F. et al. (2018). The future of stellar occultations by distant solar system bodies: perspectives from the Gaia astrometry and the deep sky surveys. Planetary and Space Science 154, 59-62 (arXiv:1903.00723)
note: Read from the arXiv text. Source of the statement that occultation positions receive the largest weights in NIMA and of the LSST astrometric accuracy of about 10 mas per exposure.

title: Buie, M. W., Porter, S. B. et al. (2020). Size and shape constraints of (486958) Arrokoth from stellar occultations. AJ 159, 130 (arXiv:2001.00125)
note: Read the prediction, deployment and astrometry sections from the arXiv text. Source of the 31.4 km per mas scale, the 44 km, 14 km and 13 km cross-track uncertainties, the Monte Carlo deployment planner, the 15.5 km and 4 km station spacings, the pre-release Gaia DR2 use and the airborne clock offsets.

title: Preston, S. Steve's Asteroid Update: HELP / FAQ page (asteroidoccultation.com), last updated 2019-06-11
note: Read. Source of the Occult plot conventions: the path width as diameter divided by the sine of the star altitude, the dashed 1-sigma lines and the 68 and 95 per cent interpretation, the uncertainty ellipse, the Rank definition and the RUWE note.

title: Preston, S. Asteroid Occultation Predictions home page (asteroidoccultation.com)
note: Read on 2026-10-17. States that from 2024 the posted predictions are not the most current and that the current ones are distributed through OccultWatcher.

title: Preston, S. (2007). Asteroid Occultation Prediction Process (slides, as of summer 2007)
note: Read from the Wayback Machine copy of 2019-10-21; the live file returns 404. Pre-Gaia baseline: searchers and catalogues (Tycho-2, UCAC2, Hipparcos), OrbFit with JPL DE405, 1 arcsec default a priori RMS against 0.12 to 0.35 arcsec for high-accuracy astrometry, 13 perturbing asteroids, Dunham's event criteria, and too many 2-sigma shifts.

title: Pavlov, H. OccultWatcher home page
note: Read. Describes OccultWatcher as a Windows client that filters asteroid-occultation prediction feeds and lets observers announce their stations, and lists the feeds (IOTA Updates from Preston, OZNZ, NAmer, E.A.O.N., TNO and others).

title: Dunham, D. W. et al. (2024). 2024 Occultations of Bright Stars by Main-Belt Asteroids. RASC Observer's Handbook supplement
note: Read (pdftotext). States that the 2024 orbital elements are from JPL Horizons and star data from Gaia DR3 in Occult's catalogue, that path locations are uncertain by a few tenths of a path width, and that improved predictions are now distributed only through OccultWatcher.

title: JPL Solar System Dynamics. SBDB (Small-Body DataBase) API documentation
note: Read. The cov parameter returns the orbital covariance as a full matrix, an upper-triangular vector or its square root, at the JPL orbit-solution epoch.

title: Braga-Ribas, F., Sicardy, B., Ortiz, J. L. et al. (2014). A ring system detected around the Centaur (10199) Chariklo. Nature 508, 72-75 (arXiv:1409.7259)

title: Ortiz, J. L., Santos-Sanz, P., Sicardy, B. et al. (2017). The size, shape, density and ring of the dwarf planet Haumea from a stellar occultation. Nature 550, 219-223 (arXiv:2006.03113)

title: Sicardy, B., Tej, A., Gomes-Júnior, A. R. et al. (2024). Constraints on the evolution of the Triton atmosphere from occultations: 1989-2022. A&A 682, L24 (arXiv:2402.02476)

title: Albers, S. C. (1979). Mutual occultations of planets: 1557 to 2230. Sky & Telescope 57(3), 220-222

note: Read. Summarises Albers 1979 and adds events computed with Guide 7.0. Gives the Venus-Jupiter events of 1570, 1818, 2065 and 2123 with times, elongations, diameters and geocentric separations, and the Mercury events to 2133.

title: Gray, B. (Project Pluto). Assorted celestial events: mutual planetary events, -1000 to +6000
